title: Surveyor 7 television data printout mosaic sheet
description: NSSDC scan of a mosaic sheet printed from the original Surveyor 7 television data. Part of a set of 16 large scans covering Surveyor 7's stepped television surveys.
projection: scan of a printout sheet; not a re-projected panorama
licence: NASA-produced, public domain in the United States; credit requested
verificationNote: Downloaded and measured by the parent agent through the proxy: 200, JPEG, 3790x1954, 1,013,393 B.
notes: The strongest non-Apollo NASA surface asset found. Not a seamless panorama: the scans include film sprocket edges, greyscale calibration wedges and dots. The printed azimuth ranges on the catalogue headers inside the set cover roughly 227 degrees and wrap through 0, so a full circle exists across the set but only as separate stepped-survey frames. Label it as a historic printout scan, not a panorama.

title: Artemis II 'Earthset' from Orion
description: Earth setting behind the lunar limb, photographed from Orion during the crewed Artemis II free-return flyby. Included because it is the strongest genuine Artemis-era asset and is NOT a surface panorama.
verificationNote: Downloaded and measured by the parent agent: 200, JPEG, 3819x5092, 15,048,599 B — note this is PORTRAIT and 15 MB, which corrects a subagent report of 5568x3712 / 1,009,521 B.
notes: Not a panorama and not a landing site. Listed to keep the record straight and to correct the earlier dimension claim.

title: Luna 9 / Luna 13 / Lunokhod 1 / Lunokhod 2 re-processed panoramas (Don P. Mitchell catalogue)
description: The largest usable set of Soviet lunar surface panoramas: Luna 9 and Luna 13 partial sweeps, and the Lunokhod 1 and Lunokhod 2 horizontal and vertical pans.
credit: Sternberg Astronomical Institute; scans/processing by Don P. Mitchell
licence: All rights reserved — 'Copyright (c) 2003,2004 Don P. Mitchell. All rights reserved.' quoted from the page itself
verificationNote: Page reached (200) and the copyright line quoted verbatim by the parent agent. The individual image files were NOT re-measured: the dimensions above are the subagent's and are marked accordingly.
notes: DO NOT redistribute. Each file is a ~180 degree strip, not 360: per ISPRS XL-4 121 (2014) the horizontal cameras are 30 deg vertical by slightly more than 180 deg horizontal, 500 samples x 3000 lines, optical axis tilted 15 deg down, and two cameras on opposite sides together give the full circle. Lunokhod 2 is the demo's existing luna-21 site. Best use is a clearly credited link-out.

licence: Not stated as open; credited to Roscosmos / Russian Academy of Sciences
